A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Middle Devonian carbonate mounds and associated evaporitic beds of the Elk Point basin were deposited in a shallow, restricted, hypersaline basin with a stratified water column.

the basal laminitic and graded carbonate deposits of the Elk Point evaporitic succession were formed subaqueously by a process of seasonal precipitation of carbonate minerals in a physically and biologically stratified water mass.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the laminites of the Elk Point basin were formed in an environment of physical and chemical stratification of the bottom waters.
the laminated and graded carbonate beds are the result of subaqueous deposition in an anoxic water mass with seasonal precipitation of carbonate in the upper water stratum.
